sections.title: Buying thinking time naturally
sections.use: Use when you need a few seconds to organise your answer, so you sound thoughtful rather than hesitant.

items.example: That's a really interesting question, I don't think anyone's asked me that before.

items.phrase: Let me think about that for a second
items.example: Let me think about that for a second, because there are a couple of things that come to mind.

items.phrase: Well, to be honest with you
items.example: Well, to be honest with you, I've never given it much thought until now.

items.phrase: It's not something I've really considered before
items.example: It's not something I've really considered before, but I'd say it depends on the situation.
Where do I start? There's so much I could say about my hometown.
Now that you mention it, I do spend far too much time on my phone.

items.phrase: If I had to pick one, I'd say
items.example: If I had to pick one, I'd say my grandmother was the biggest influence on me.
How can I put this? I'm not a morning person, to put it mildly.

sections.title: Giving opinions
sections.use: Use to state your view clearly and add nuance, from strong views to softer, more balanced ones.

items.example: Personally, I'd say that online classes will never fully replace face-to-face teaching.
From my point of view, public transport should be much cheaper than it is.

items.phrase: I'm firmly of the opinion that
items.example: I'm firmly of the opinion that children should learn to cook at school.
As far as I'm concerned, a good teacher matters more than a fancy classroom.
I tend to think that people were more sociable before smartphones came along.

items.phrase: I couldn't agree more with the idea that
items.example: I couldn't agree more with the idea that volunteering builds character.

items.phrase: I'm a bit torn on this one
items.example: I'm a bit torn on this one, because technology has helped us but also made us lazy.
If you ask me, most people underestimate how much a short walk can clear your head.

sections.title: Hedging and speculating
sections.use: Use for Part 3 questions about the future, causes and effects, or things you can't be certain about.

items.example: It's quite likely that more people will work from home in the coming decade.
I wouldn't be surprised if paper books became a luxury item one day.
It could well be that younger people value experiences more than possessions.
I suppose it depends on how much support families get from the government.
Generally speaking, people in big cities tend to be busier and less patient.
By and large, I think the benefits of social media outweigh the downsides.
I'd imagine that most teachers find marking the hardest part of the job.
To some extent, technology has made us more connected, but not necessarily closer.

sections.title: Comparing and contrasting
sections.use: Use to compare past and present, two groups of people, or two options in Part 3.

items.example: Compared with my parents' generation, we have far more choice about our careers.
Older people often prefer calling, whereas teenagers mostly send voice messages.

items.phrase: On the one hand... on the other hand
items.example: On the one hand, cars are convenient, but on the other hand, they cause a lot of pollution.
The main difference is that people used to stay in one job for life.
In contrast to the city, life in my village feels slow and quiet.
Learning online is not nearly as engaging as sitting in a real classroom.
Cycling is cheap and healthy. Having said that, it's not much fun in the rain.
Similarly, many young people nowadays prefer renting to buying a home.

sections.title: Describing past experiences
sections.use: Use to tell short, vivid stories in Part 1 and Part 2, with natural time markers and feelings.

items.phrase: It was a few years back when
items.example: It was a few years back when I first moved abroad to study.
I'll never forget the time my bike broke down miles from home.
Looking back on it, that failure taught me more than any success.

items.phrase: At the time, I didn't realise that
items.example: At the time, I didn't realise that the advice would change my whole career.
To my surprise, the whole class stood up and clapped when I finished.
Before I knew it, three hours had gone by and the sun had set.
It turned out that the stranger lived on the same street as me.
Ever since then, I've made a point of double-checking my bags before a trip.

sections.title: Describing people and places
sections.use: Use for Part 2 cue cards about a person, a place or a building, to add detail beyond basic adjectives.

items.phrase: He's the kind of person who
items.example: He's the kind of person who always remembers your birthday.

items.phrase: She has a real knack for
items.example: She has a real knack for making difficult topics feel simple.

items.phrase: What really struck me about him was
items.example: What really struck me about him was how patient he was with everyone.
It's tucked away in a quiet side street, so most tourists never find it.

items.phrase: The place has a laid-back atmosphere
items.example: The place has a laid-back atmosphere, so you can stay for hours without feeling rushed.
It's surrounded by hills, which makes the view absolutely breathtaking.
He comes across as quite strict, but he's actually very kind.
It's famous for its night market, which gets packed at weekends.

sections.title: Band 7+ idioms by theme
sections.use: Use one or two idioms where they fit naturally. Too many sounds forced, so keep them for a clear point.

items.phrase: Work and study: burn the midnight oil
items.example: Before my exams, I had to burn the midnight oil for a whole week.

items.phrase: Work and study: a piece of cake
items.example: The listening section was a piece of cake, but the reading was much harder.

items.phrase: Time: in the nick of time
items.example: We got to the station in the nick of time and just caught the last train.
I was over the moon when I found out I'd got the scholarship.

items.phrase: Money: cost an arm and a leg
items.example: Living in the city centre costs an arm and a leg these days.
Missing that flight was a blessing in disguise, because I met my future business partner at the airport.
I'm a creature of habit, so I have the same breakfast every single day.
I'm still on the fence about whether to study abroad or stay at home.

sections.title: Linking and extending answers
sections.use: Use to add a reason, an example or a contrast, so your answers grow naturally beyond one sentence.

items.example: The reason for that is that I grew up near the sea.
For instance, my neighbour started a small food bank last year.
It's cheap, and on top of that, it's much faster than driving.
What's more, you meet people from all sorts of backgrounds.
That's partly because I never learned to swim as a child.
I can't stand crowds, which is why I avoid the shopping centre at weekends.
I love the city. Mind you, I wouldn't want to live there forever.
Come to think of it, my best memories all involve food.
